G7300.definition:
1.  to count throughout, number  , Lat.  enumerare , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2.  to count out, pay in ready   money, Lat.  numeratim solvere , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7301.definition:
1. of objects,  to be quite enough for, suffice for  , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; πρός τι (Xenophon Historicus):  absolute   to suffice, be sufficient  , (Euripides) 
2.  impersonal , ἐξαρκεῖ  it is enough for, suffices for  , with  dative  pers., (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
3. of persons,  to be satisfied with, to be a match for  , with  dative , (Euripides):—;with  participle   to be content with having  , (Euripides) (ML)

G7303.definition:
1.  to hang upon, to make dependent upon  , with  genitive , (Plutarch): also in Mid., (Euripides) 
2. Pass.,  future  in  middle  form -αρτήσομαι,  perfect  -ήρτημαι:—;  to be hung upon, hang upon  , χειρός (Euripides) 
3.  to depend upon, be dependent upon, be attached to  , σοῦ γὰρ ἐξηρτήμεθα (Euripides) 
4. of countries,  to border upon  , τινος (Plutarch) 
5.  to be hung up   or  exposed to view  , (Thucydides) 
6.  perfect   passive   participle , with  accusative  rei,  having   a thing  hung on one, be furnished with  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7304.definition:
1.  to begin with, make a beginning of  , Lat.  auctor esse , with  genitive , ἐξῆρχε γόοιο (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;so in Mid., ἐξήρχετο βουλῆς (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. with  accusative , βουλὰς ἐξάρχων (Iliad by Homer);—;also ἐξάρχειν or ἐξάρχεσθαι παιᾶνά τινι  to begin   a hymn to one,  address   it to him, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7306.definition: Lat.  exhedra , a hall or  arcade   in the gymnasia, a sort of  cloister  , (Euripides) (ML)

G7309.definition:
1. occurs in (Homer):—;  to drive out from  , ἄντρου ἐξήλασε μῆλα (Odyssey by Homer);  absolute   to drive afield  , of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer):—;especially  to drive out   or  expel from   a place, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
2.  to drive out   horses or chariots, (Iliad by Homer): Mid.  to drive out one's   horses, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); so, ἐξελαύνειν στρατόν  to lead out   an army, (Herdotus Historicus): hence 
3.  intransitive   to march out  , (Herdotus Historicus):  to drive   or  ride out  , (Thucydides) 
4.  to knock out  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
5.  to beat out   metals, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7310.definition:
1.  to unroll  , (Euripides): metaphorically   to unfold  , Lat.  explicare , (Euripides) 
2. of any rapid motion, ἴχνος ἐξ. ποδός  to evolve the mazy   dance, (Euripides):—;hence  intransitive   to wheel about  , (Plutarch) 
3. as military term, = ἀναπτύσσειν, Lat.  explicare , to extend the front by bringing up the rear men,  to deploy  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  to draw off  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7311.definition:
1.  to vomit forth, disgorge  , (Odyssey by Homer):—; metaphorically   to disgorge   ill-gotten gear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  absolute   to vomit, be sick  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7312.definition:
1.  to work out, make completely, finish off, bring to perfection  , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2.  to accomplish, perform, achieve   a work, (Sophocles Tragicus); κακὸν ἐξ. τινα  to work   him mischief, (Herdotus Historicus):—;as Pass., ἔργον ἐστὶν ἐξειργασμένον (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐπ᾽ ἐξεργασμένοισι after  the deed   had been done, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  to work at  : as Pass., ἀγροὶ εὖ ἐξεργασμένοι well  cultivated   lands, (Herdotus Historicus); [ ἡ γῆ] ἐξείργασται (Thucydides) 
4.  to undo, destroy, overwhelm, ruin  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;as Pass., ἐξειργάσμεθα  we are undone  , (Euripides) (ML)

G7313.definition: Pass., of rivers,  to empty themselves  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7315.definition: to make quite desolate, leave destitute, abandon  , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ. γένυν δράκοντος  making   it  destitute   of teeth, (Euripides):—;Pass.  to be left destitute  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7316.definition:
1.  to creep out of  , ἔκ τινος (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  absolute   to creep out   or  forth  , (Sophocles Tragicus); of an army, οὐ ταχὺ ἐξέρπει (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7319.definition:
1.  to stand out   or  project from  , τινός (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  absolute   to stand out, appear  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7320.definition:
1.  a statement, narrative  , (Thucydides) 
2.  explanation, interpretation  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7321.definition:
1.  one who leads on, an adviser  , Lat.  auctor , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  an expounder, interpreter  , of oracles, dreams, omens, and sacred customs, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7331.definition: Dep.  to propitiate  , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7334.definition: Dep.  to ride out   or  away  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7336.definition:
1.  to make equal   or  even bring to a level with  , Lat.  exaequare , τινά or τί τινι (Sophocles Tragicus):—; Mid.  to make oneself equal  , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;Pass.  to be   or  become equal  , τινι (Plato Philosophus), etc.;  to be a match for, to rival  , τινι (Thucydides) 
2.  to put on a level  , τοὺς πολίτας (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  intransitive   to be equal   or  like  , μητρὶ δ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐξισοῖ  acts   in no way  like   a mother, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ. τοῖς ἄλλοις (Thucydides): so in Pass., (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7341.definition: of   or  belonging to an exit  :—;as  Substantive , ἐξόδιον (i.e. μέλος);  the finale of a tragedy  , (Plutarch):  metaphorically   a catastrophe  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7342.definition: to build completely, finish a building  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7344.definition:
1.  intransitive , of a ship,  to run aground   or  ashore  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  transitive   to run   (a ship)  aground  :—; metaphorically   to drive headlong  , (Euripides) (ML)

G7345.definition:
1.  to destroy utterly  , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
2. Mid., with  perfect  2 ἐξόλωλα,  to perish utterly  , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G7348.definition:
1. attic for ἐξόπιθεν, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. as  preposition  with  genitive , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 ἐξοπίσω, αδv. (ML)

G7349.definition: to arm completely, accoutre  , (Herdotus Historicus): —;Mid. and Pass.  to arm   or  accoutre oneself  , (Euripides):  to get under arms, stand in armed array  , (Euripides):—; generally, ἐξωπλισμένος  fully prepared, all ready  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7350.definition:
1.  to send forth, send to war  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐξ. τὴν ναῦν  to start   the ship,  set   it  agoing  , (Thucydides):—;Pass.  to set out, start  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; of arrows,  to spring from   the bow, (Euripides) 
2.  to excite to action, urge on  , (Euripides) 
3.  intransitive , like Pass.,  to set out, start  , of a ship, (Odyssey by Homer): with  genitive   to set out from  , (Euripides):—; metaphorically   to break out  , of a disease, (Sophocles Tragicus); σφοδρὸς ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι ἐφορμήσειε eager in all that  he attempted  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7354.definition: to break out into insolence, to run riot, wax wanton  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐξ. ἐς τόδε  to come to   this  pitch of insolence  , (Thucydides): with an  adjective   neuter , παντοῖα ἐξ.  to commit   all kinds of  violence  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7357.definition:
1.  a bringing in, supplying  , (Thucydides) 
2.  a bringing in to one's aid, introduction  , (Thucydides) 
3.  a drawing on, alluring  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7360.definition:
1.  a means of defence  : in  plural   battlements  , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;in  singular   the battlements, parapet  , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally,  a defence, protection  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7362.definition: intransitive   to turn back upon   one,  wheel round   and  return to the charge  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; so in Pass., (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7364.definition: to have come back, to return  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7365.definition:
1.  to bloom, be in flower  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2.  metaphorically  of  any thing that forms on the surface  , as a salt crust, (Herdotus Historicus); the down on fruit, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: generally,  to be upon the surface, shew itself, appear plainly  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  to be bright  , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G7366.definition:
1.  from above, above  , (Euripides) 
2. οἱ ἐπ.  men of former time  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7374.definition:
1.  a commander  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. the Roman  praefectus  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7375.definition: to discharge at  , with  dative , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7376.definition:
1.  to be upon  , with  dative , (Iliad by Homer); but in Prose with  preposition , ἐπὶ τοῦ καταστρώματος (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ ταῖς οἰκίαις (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  to be set upon  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of rewards and penalties,  to be affixed   or  attached  , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. of Time,  to be hereafter, remain  , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπεσσόμενοι ἄνθρωποι generations  to come  , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;also  to be at hand  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  to be set over  , Lat.  praeesse , τισι (Herdotus Historicus) 
5.  to be added, be over and above  , of numbers, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7379.definition:
1.  to buoy up with hope, to cheat with false hopes  , (Thucydides) 
2.  intransitive  = ἐλπίζω, (Euripides) (ML)

G7380.definition: to drive against, drive home  , ἔγχος (Iliad by Homer); ἐπέρεισε δὲ ἶν᾽ ἀπέλεθρον  put   vast strength  to   it, (Homer):—; ἐπ. τὴν φάλαγγά τινι  to bring the whole force of   the phalanx against, (Plutarch):—;Mid., λαίφη προτόνοις ἐπερειδόμεναι  staying their   sails on ropes, (Euripides):—;Pass.  to lean   or  bear upon  , τινι (Aristophanes Comicus):  absolute   to resist with all one's force  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7382.definition:
1.  annual, yearly  , (Herdotus Historicus): ἐπέτειοι τὴν φύσιν  changeful   as the seasons, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  annual, lasting for a year  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7384.definition:
1. Dep. 
2.  to pray   or  make a vow   to a deity, with  dative , (Homer), etc.:—;with  infinitive   to pray to   one  that . .  , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. :—;with  accusative  rei,  to pray for  , (Aeschulus Tragicus): also, with  accusative   cognate , ἐπ. λιτάς (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3.  to imprecate   a curse  upon  , τί τινι (Aeschulus Tragicus); with  infinitive , ἐπεύχομαι [ αὐτῷ] παθεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus):  absolute   to utter imprecations  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  to glory over  , τινι (Iliad by Homer) 
5.  to boast that  , with  infinitive , (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G7385.definition:
1.  listening   or  giving ear to   a thing, with  genitive , (Aeschulus Tragicus); also with  dative , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  within hearing, within ear-shot  , εἰς ἐπήκοον (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7387.definition: a stepping upon, approaching: a means of approach, access  , (Plato Philosophus); εἴς τινα ποιεῖσθαι ἐπ. to find a  means of attacking   one, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7388.definition:
1.  one who mounts   or  embarks;   
2. ἐπιβάται, οἱ,  the soldiers on board   ship,  the fighting men  , as opposite to the rowers and seamen, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  a merchant on board ship, supercargo  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  the fighting man   in a chariot, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7390.definition:
1.  to plan   or  contrive against  , κακὸν πόλει (Tyrtaeus Elegiacus); θάνατόν τινι (Herdotus Historicus):—;with  dative  pers. only,  to plot against, lay snares for  , τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷ πλήθει (Aristophanes Comicus);—; absolute , οὑπιβουλεύων  the conspirer  , (Sophocles Tragicus): —;with  accusative  rei only,  to plan secretly, scheme, plot  , τὸν ἔκπλουν (Thucydides) 
2. with  dative  rei,  to form designs upon, aim at  , πρήγμασι μεγάλοισι (Herdotus Historicus); τυραννίδι (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with  infinitive   to purpose   or  design to   do, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. Pass., with  future   middle  -εύσομαι: aor1 -εβουλεύθην:—;  to have plots formed against one, to be the object of plots  , (Thucydides) 
5. of things,  to be designed against  , πρᾶγμα, ὃ τοῖς θεοῖς ἐπιβουλεύεται (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ ἐπιβουλευόμενα  plots  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7391.definition: plotting against  , τινι (Plato Philosophus):  treacherous  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7393.definition: = Lat.  connubium , the right of intermarriage between states, (Xenophon Historicus):—;generally,  intermarriage  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7394.definition:
1.  to laugh approvingly  , Lat.  arrideo , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
2. = ἐπεγγελάω, (Lucian) (ML)

G7397.definition:
1.  an arbiter, umpire, judge  , with  genitive  rei, (Plato Philosophus); ἐπ. τῆς τιμῆς an appraiser, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. = συγγνώμων,  pardoning  , τινί (Moschus Bucolicus) (ML)
